name: Anti-apartheid movement
title: The story of the anti-apartheid movement

text: More than 75 years ago, South Africa's government began apartheid, laws that kept people apart by race.
Every person was sorted by race, and each group had to live in its own areas.
src: The National Party wins power and begins to build apartheid into law / on the programme of apartheid, “separateness”
classified every person by race / assigned separate residential areas to each group

text: People of every colour joined together to work for one South Africa where everyone could vote.
Steve Biko, a medical student, urged Black people to build their own groups.
src: Opposition to apartheid joined African, Indian, coloured and white South Africans / a single, democratic South Africa for all its people / votes for all
Steve Biko (1946–1977), a medical student / build their own organisations

text: Police shot protesters at Sharpeville, and the main groups against apartheid were banned.
Nelson Mandela, a leader of the struggle, was sent to prison for life.
src: Police kill 69 protesters at Sharpeville, and the ANC and the PAC are banned
Nelson Mandela and seven others are sentenced to life imprisonment in the Rivonia Trial

text: Churches gave the movement shelter and a voice, through leaders such as Desmond Tutu.
Around the world, people refused to buy South African goods or to play sport against its teams.
src: The churches gave the movement shelter and a voice: Desmond Tutu
a worldwide movement of consumer, sports and cultural boycotts

text: Then, 35 years ago, the leader F. W. de Klerk lifted the bans, and Mandela walked free after 27 years.
Four years later, people of all races voted together for the first time, and Mandela became president.
src: F. W. de Klerk unbans the liberation movements, and Mandela is freed after 27 years
South Africans of all races voted together for the first time / Mandela becomes president

text: Robben Island, where Mandela was held for eighteen years, is now a museum.
Everyone can vote now, but the gap between rich and poor built under apartheid lasted long after it.
src: eighteen of them on Robben Island / Robben Island has become a museum and a World Heritage Site
the end of legal racial discrimination and votes for all / the economic inequalities built under apartheid long outlasted it
